tagline: Two river gorges, with a mountain gap between.
intro: From Highlands, the byway follows US 64 and NC 28 down the Cullasaja Gorge toward Franklin, past one waterfall after another. Bridal Veil Falls actually comes off a tributary creek, and Dry Falls lets visitors walk behind it without getting wet.

Beyond Franklin, the road climbs west through Wayah Gap, at 4,180 feet, on its way to Nantahala Lake and Aquone. From there it follows the Nantahala River down through its gorge to the end of the byway at Lauada.

moments.title: Quarry Falls
moments.text: Locals call this small waterfall beside US 64 Bust-Your-Butt Falls; the large, deep pool at its foot is a swimming place in warm weather.

moments.title: Pendergrass Building
moments.text: Built in 1904 and left almost unaltered, this two-story brick store on Main Street sold goods until 1975 and now holds the Macon County Historical Society and Museum.

moments.title: Nantahala Outdoor Center
moments.text: The Appalachian Trail crosses the Nantahala on a bridge next to the outfitter, which opened in 1972 in the old Tote 'N Tarry Motel.
